notes.title: Squad 51 Comes to Nintendo Switch on March 16th!
notes.content:
It’s a bird! It’s a plane! It’s… an alien spacecraft?! Squad 51 vs. The Flying Saucers, a cinematic 2D shoot ‘em up, is soaring onto the Nintendo Switch on [b]March 16th[/b]. Band together with a group of rebels and claim extraterrestrial victory! Director Zarog and the malevolent Vega Corporation are no match for a pair of joy-cons.

[previewyoutube=5wdehgkbrwA;full][/previewyoutube]

Visitors from the stars have arrived on Earth with the promise of a bright future for all humankind. The facade quickly falls, revealing the true evil nature of the intergalactic Vega Corporation and their horrific leader, Director Zarog. Through humanity’s oppression, hope rises with the birth of a rebel cause. Step into the cockpit as Lieutenant Kaya, and lead Squadron 51 on a campaign to take down the Vega Corporation once and for all!

Squad 51 vs. The Flying Saucers transports players to the glorious days of the 1950s through an authentic black and white cinematic aesthetic. Take control of four different aircrafts, all with their own unique set of weapons and abilities. Fly through eleven levels and take down the galactic invaders across arctic mountains, lush forests, and battered cities. With cooperative play, a friend can join in at any time to help you take down the waves of enemies and ruthless bosses. 

Take flight and save all of humanity on the go when Squad 51 vs. The Flying Saucers barrel rolls onto Nintendo Switch on March 16th.

[b]Features: [/b]
[list]
[*] Classic gameplay: Squad 51 vs. The Flying Saucers is a shoot ‘em up game with four different aircrafts to play and set up with special weapons.
[*] Cinematic experience: Glorious black-and-white aesthetics, live-action FMV sequences and dubbed voices will tell the story of the battle between the squadron and Director Zarog’s alien supremacy.
[*] Eleven levels: Fight against enemy ships and bosses in many different environments - snowy mountains, forests, cityscapes, and many others.
[*] Dynamic difficulty: Rookie or veteran, Squad 51 vs. The Flying Saucers supports dynamic difficulty which allows every pilot to enjoy the fight.
[*] Multiplayer: Feeling lonely shooting down aliens? Invite a friend! A second player can enter a level at any time. Earn points with your friend and unlock new special weapons and upgrades together.
[/list]

notes.title: ATTACK FROM PLANET TRIVIA #05 - SHOOT'EM UP! A Brief Flight Through the Genre
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38472313/3b79817703fc14c45c039825fd59d80150308201.png[/img]

If you think about the Cathode-ray Tube Amusement Device, the first electronic game ever released in 1947, you reach the conclusion that the Shoot ‘em Up (or simply SHMUP) might be the oldest videogame genre ever. From the late 1970’s to the early 1990’s, this was one of the genres that dominated the golden age of arcades with classics like “Space Invaders” and “Asteroids”. It includes a large variety of styles, like the chaotic “bullet hell”, in which projectiles are coming from everywhere in different formations, to the “run ’n gun” in which the character is on foot instead of controlling an aircraft.

In the 20th century, the genre lost its widespread popularity, with studios and gamers aiming at more complex gameplay or hyperrealistic graphics and narratives. It was only in recent years that a sense of nostalgia emerged from indie studios with retrogaming and new releases trying to bring back the simple and straightforward characteristics of this beloved kind.

in this update, we’d like to present to you (or maybe remind you of) the SHMUPs that have close relations with “Squadron 51”.

[h1]GRADIUS (1985)[/h1]

One of the most classic shooters of the Arcade era was introduced by Konami in 1985 and stablished some of the base concepts of the genre: sidescrolling; the weapon bar; customization; power up itens and specials. It became a powerful franchise, inspiring spin-off series, parodies and copycats. The narrative is simple: you take control of the iconic aircraft known as Vic Viper and must survive alien attacks to save the universe. “Shoot the core!” says the series’ call to action, referencing the pulsating inner energy chamber, the weak spot of nearly all Gradius’ bosses. Most of these concepts are also found in our “Squadron 51”, since Gradius was one of our major influences.
[previewyoutube=S1UBwtYrHUI;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]R-TYPE (1987)[/h1]

“R-Type” was released by Irem in 1987 in arcade platforms. While the gameplay was obviously inspired by Gradius, the monstrous aesthetic was influenced by the works of the artist H. R. Giger, that has also served as basis for the Alien movie franchise. In the time of its release, “R-Type” raised the bar for SHMUPs in terms of building atmosphere, with its bio-mechanical imagery, a large variety of enemies and mind-blowing difficulty.
[previewyoutube=BRFRr_SrrvM;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]THUNDER FORCE (1983 - present)[/h1]

Another free-roaming scrolling shooter franchise well known for kids of the 90’s is Thunder Force, created by female developer Kotori Yoshimura. Even if the original was a hit in the Arcade machines of the 80’s, it was in the consoles that this shooter found its niche. It had all the elements a Shmup fan looks for: thrilling action, challenging difficulty and screen-filling weaponry. One unique feature of the game is that the levels don’t just scroll from left to right, but also back and forward, up and down. The trick, as always, is to memorize the patterns.
[previewyoutube=1zqRIBWcNGQ;full][/previewyoutube]

SINE MORA (2012)

This dieselpunk shooter was one of the benchmarks for the platforms and SHMUPs revival during the 2010’s. Featuring incredible set pieces, it takes all the classic concepts of the genre and adds another thrilling element to it: a ticking clock, that makes the player even more tense than most bullet-hell. This game features a more complex story than most arcade shooters, with all its dystopian narrative, monster bosses and Starfox-inspired furry like characters. This is something we’re also aiming to achieve in our game. Though we’re working in one of the simplest of games’ genres, we want to tell a rich and flashy story in our own way.
[previewyoutube=DaO1djQMhF4;full][/previewyoutube]

CUPHEAD (2017)

When “Cuphead" was released in 2017, “Squadron 51”’s concept was already solid, and the development was in its early stages, so we can’t say that it was a fundamental influence in our process. However, that didn’t stop media and gamers from comparing the two projects, not only for its chaotic bullet-hell scenarios, but also for the research and fidelity to the vintage sources that inspired both games. While “Squadron 51” intends to give the player a full immersion in the 1950’s sci-fi vibes, “Cuphead”, created by the Moldenhauer brothers, is built around an incredible research on 1930’s animation’s aesthetic. A resounding success for critics and gamers, this ode for the Golden Age cartoons gets you hooked on its beautiful hand-drawn environments and bosses and on the challenging difficulty, based on the players’ skills in memorizing patterns and willingness to learn.
[previewyoutube=NN-9SQXoi50;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: THEM! Meet Cast and Crew #04 - Music & Sound!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38472313/a9469c2a162f37d13743aefb48ce04c633efa9ff.png[/img]

On this week’s “Them”, we’ll meet the crew responsible for Squadron 51’s unique sound experience!

[h1]PRODUCTION SOUND CREW
[/h1]

We’ve trusted the on-set recording of our FMV to a talented team of regular collaborators on Fehorama Filmes. With their experience acquired in hundreds of projects, from short films to feature films and TV series, the Production Sound Mixer Fábio Duarte and Boom Operators Tiago Ruppenthal and Guilherme Cássio made sure that everything was perfectly recorded during the six days of our shooting.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38472313/107dbf2a78d081e5b29e651bfe8769a985e25b52.jpg[/img]

[h1]SOUND DESIGN
[/h1]

The crew responsible for editing and mixing the audible experience of our game, in all its forms, from the sound effects to the voice acting, is KF Studios. Named after its founder, Kiko Ferraz, the company has worked in more than 70 feature films. They’re also responsible for the sound of a number of TV shows for channels such as HBO, TV Globo, Discovery Channel, History Channel and Fox. Though SQ51 is KF’s first sound design for a game, it’s certainly not their first experience on the universe of videogames. With a cast of over 250 voices, they have been localizing and dubbing games in brazillian portuguese for years. Among the more than 20 projects, there are big franchises such as Star Wars and Battlefield. In their own words, they believe in the power of sound to sensibilize and inspire, and that’s what they’re doing in Squadron 51. For this project, they’re not only researching the best sound FX for the aircrafts and explosions, but also studying sound filters to make our game feel like a 1950’s sci-fi B movie, in both the cutscenes and the gameplay. [/h1]

Our composer, arranger and orchestrator Renan Franzen is a fan of sci-fi films and games since he was a kid, and we’re glad to count with his passion for the genre in our project. notes.title: ATTACK FROM PLANET TRIVIA #04
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38472313/d249653f2fa59371d9d818d2a1153c14151ea1b4.png[/img]

One of the biggest risks we’re taking is to fully embrace the concept of live-action cinematics. This is certainly not new in the history of videogames, but it became an unusual choice in recent decades. We’ve decided to stick with the “retro” charm of using real actors and on-set action to tell the story of the resistance against Director Zarog.

From arcade machines in the 1970’s to the peak of the point-and-click adventure games, the live-action FMV has became quite a trend in the 1990s. Let’s take a look at some examples that helped us solidify our confidence in the choices we’ve made in “Squadron 51”.

[h1]Sewer Shark[/h1]

“Sewer Shark” is considered to be the first game on a console to feature a full-motion video gameplay. Afterwards, it was also released in a CD-Rom format, making it one of the most widely available games of the early 90s. In this SEGA rail-shooter, we’re presented to a militar dystopia, the player assumes the role of a rookie pilot to exterminated mutated creatures that are inhabiting the sewers.
[previewyoutube=aIb3armCCXA;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]The 7th Guest[/h1]

“The 7th Guest” is a point & click adventure developed by Trilobyte, originally released in 1993, and became a cult classic ever since. The game takes place in the past, and the story is told through a series of ghostly flashbacks shot in a very 90s way. The mansion is presented as a series of intricate 3D renderings of interior, with pre-rendered animated transitions between locations. Along the way, the player watches non-interactive in-game cutscenes, which use full-motion video (FMV) superimposed upon the backgrounds.
[previewyoutube=Zd36KUgAyxQ;full][/previewyoutube]

Wing Commander IV: The Price of Freedom

The Wing Commander franchise was a mark in the history of videogames for a variety of reasons, and its fourth installment is no different. The space flight simulator developed by Origin Systems featured the live-action sequences starring no other than Mark Hamill himself and also well-respected actors such as Malcom McDowell and John Rhys-Davies. For this production, instead of using blue-screen techniques seen in the previous game and in most of videogames, they built real sets. As a result, at the time of its release, Wing Commander IV became the most expensive video game ever made.
[previewyoutube=rYAcyeQQlq8;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]Command and Conquer[/h1]

Maybe the campiest franchise to use FMV as a trade-mark, the real-time strategy game is gaining sequels and remasters to this day, and most of them betting on using live-action cutscenes even if that’s a trend the industry widely abandoned. But the campy charm attracted cult actors such as Tim Curry, Peter Stormare, Udo Kier and Ray Wise to give arthouse legitimacy to the sequences, and the cheesy Cold-War paranoia feels are everywhere, as you can check below on these Command And Conquer: Red Alert III scenes.
[previewyoutube=at5sM6jdRNg;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

[h1]Quantum Break[/h1]

In the 2010’s, triple-A games became increasingly hyperrealistic, giving cinematographic vibes to its complex narratives, as you can see in renowned games such as the "Uncharted" and “The Last of Us” franchises, both from the studio Naughty Dog. On the verge of that, a smaller trend has been trying to retrieve the charm of the live-action FMV in a more serious tone. The epitome of that is seen in the ambitious Microsoft project “Quantum Break”, the time travel mystery that combines a high octane action 3D person shooter with a sci-fi thriller TV show. What makes “Quantum Break” unique is that the companion piece is optional, but the player who chooses to watch the “episodes” is presented with strategies and insights that highly impact the gameplay.
[previewyoutube=XWhg_1lLA1k;full][/previewyoutube]

If you’re still curious about the subject, you can check the Netflix Series' "High Score", about the history of the videogame industry. In the fifth episode, you'll see the very beginning of the merge between  videogames and film industries when two developers had a mission to make a game within a year and decided to shoot real actors to be their actual playable characters in their upcoming fighting game called "Mortal Kombat". The episode also tells the time that a visual effects specialist from Hollywood had an idea for a horror game which would look like a movie, but the player could choose which scenes would happen and modify the narrative in "Night Trap". This two games stirred such controversy in the USA that it led to the 1993 Congressional hearings, pushing for the creation of the Entertainment Software Ratings Board (ESRB).


To learn more about FMV, check the following sites:

https://fmvworld.com/games.html.

https://www.giantbomb.com/full-motion-video/3015-604/games/

notes.title: THEM! Meet Cast and Crew #03
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38472313/348c091bfe2f8af5109c6ee94ee92a1919f45e84.png[/img]

You've met the dreadful extraterrestrial villains, now it's time for you to meet the valiant heroes of our Squadron 51! A diverse cast of actors with very different backgrounds constitutes the group responsible for freeing humanity from the oppressive forces.

LIUTENANT KAYA (KAYA RODRIGUES)

Let's start with the one and only Liutenant Kaya, the protagonist of our story, and the one who pilots the aircrafts controlled by players during the gameplay. She's a very skilled pilot of "Foxtrot", one of the subsections of Squadron 51. The character was named after its actress, Kaya Rodrigues. Kaya is not only an actress with experience in film, television and theater, but also a singer and a very energetic "carnavalesca" (name given for the artists who lead Carnaval parades). You can see her on action in comedy sitcoms like "Necropolis" and "Alce & Alice", both of them available on Netflix Brazil, and also in high-profile feature films, such as Berlinale winner queer drama "Hard Paint" (2018) and upcoming Sundance flick "The Pink Cloud" (2021). You can check the video for her latest single below:

CAPTAIN ISHIRO (MARCELO EGUCHI)

Also on the Liutenant Kaya's division is Captain Ishiro, the leader of Foxtrot. He was named after famous japanese filmmaker Ishirô Honda, the father of "Godzilla" (1954) and responsible for multiple Kaijuu films of the 50's and 60's, such as "Rodan" (1956) and "Mothra" (1961). He's played by Marcelo Eguchi, who has little experience as an actor outside of advertising commercials (he was in more than 30 of those), but has plenty of practice in other areas. Son of a Japanese couple, Eguchi represents the very strong Japan's presence in Brazil, result of decades of immigration, which is not a very well known fact outside of Brazil. Very much connected to asian culture, Eguchi is a assiduous budhist, a very skilled martial artist, not only in Karate, but also a black belt in Taekwondo, and owner of a Sushi restaurant for 10 years now. He's also a skater and a musician, versed in a variety of instruments, such as guitar, bass, saxophone, flute, harmonica and percussion and use to play in an Emocore band called Coopet.

CAPTAIN ZEFERINA (PAULA SOUZA)

The other important division is team Bravo. This one is led by the fierce Captain Zeferina, who’s not only a pilot, but also Squadron 51’s official archer. Her name is a homage to Zeferina, a warrior who lived in Salvador in the 19th Century. Brought from Angola to Brazil as a slave, she struggled for freedom and founded “Quilombo do Urubu”, an important resistance spot for abolitionist fight in our country. The actress responsible for embodying her strength is Paula Souza, who’s been an actress for 23 years now, withe experience in theater, advertising, music videos, TV shows and films. Recently, she was in the awarded short films “Quero ir para Los Angeles” and “Fragmentos ao Vento, 1945”, and also on the upcoming thriller series “O Complexo”. You can follow her on her Instagram page @atrizpaulasouzaoficial.

AIR MARSHALL LAMARCA (ADRIANE AZEVEDO)

Occupying the highest rank in the group is Air Marshall Lamarca, the respectful leader who flies the Camelia, Squadron’s patrol bomber. She’s also named after a brazillian historical figure, Carlos Lamarca, a deserted Army Captain who became one of the biggest anti-fascist leaderships during the Military Dictatorship in Brazil. Here, she’s played by Adriane Azevedo, who’s been acting in theater plays since 1982 and won multiple awards for her performances throughout the decades. She was the wife of the late João França, who played Major Ivan (you can read more about him in our special update, here: https://bit.ly/35RjdNb). Adriane dedicates her life to culture, since she’s also a theater producer, director and a devoted teacher. You can read more about her in her official website www.adrianeazevedo.blogspot.com.

LIUTENANT VANNUCCHI (RODOLFO RUSCHEINKSY)

Last, but not least, Air Marshall’s Lamarca right hand in the Camelia, Lieutenant Vannuchi, who’s a skilled pilot and operates radio communication in the aircraft. His name is also based on the left-wing resistance of the 1970s, student leader and eco-activist Alexandre Vannuchi Leme, who mysteriously disappeared at 22 years old in the midst of one of the most violent moments in the dictatorship. To play Lieutenant Vannucchi, we chose one of our regular collaborators in Fehorama Filmes, Rodolfo Ruscheinksy. Rodolfo is an actor, filmmaker and an impressively gifted dancer, known for his comic timing in works like “Necrópoles”, “Proibido para Maiores” and “Paralelo 30”, in addition to his dramatic talent seen in the recent drama series “A Benção”. Learn about his work on his official website https://rodolforuscheinsky.wixsite.com/rodolfo

notes.title: ATTACK FROM PLANET TRIVIA #03
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38472313/38f4410a774d8265a76ea6206275e72a4f147b67.png[/img]

If you’re reading this update you probably already know that, but our main inspiration for “Squadron 51” is, obviously, the science-fiction of the nuclear era that captures the Cold War anxieties in the form of imaginative stories and crazy special effects. It’s estimated that more than 500 sci-fi films were released between 1948 and 1962.

Extraterrestrials are part of popular imagination for centuries, but in this post-war time, with the chance of happening a nuclear holocaust, the fear of a communist invasion in America and the crazy space race that was taking place between USA and USSR, those elements of alien spaceships, mind control and radioactive monsters acquired new meanings.

In appropriating this iconography in the context of a game produced in Brazil, we are re-signifying them within our experience as a colonized country. Discover some of the main films that inspired “Squadron 51”, both aesthetically and thematically.

[h1]PLAN 9 FROM OUTER SPACE (1959)[/h1]

Well, let’s start with the one named as “the worst film ever made”, by the infamous director Ed Wood. Released in 1959, the film’s confusing plot involves an alien invasion, ghouls and grave robbers, and features horror icons like Vampira and the great Bela Lugosi, who died during production. Combining elements from science-fiction, atompunk and gothic horror, the film did not have the budget that the scripts’ epic ambitions required, but it got made anyway. The flying saucers resembled paper plates glued together and you can easily see the strings. There’s so much crazy details concerning Plan 9’s production and so much cult following around it that we can’t even start to tell all of it here, but you can check it out in Tim Burton’s Ed Wood (1994) starring Johnny Depp as the failing director or in one of the many documentaries made about the subject.
[previewyoutube=aiZp2sXkVUg;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]EARTH VS. FLYING SAUCERS (1956)[/h1]

Another classic B-movie featuring the iconic plate-shaped alien aircrafts similar to those you see in “Squadron 51”. “Earth vs. Flying Saucers” is known mostly for the stop-motion effects achieved by the legendary Ray Harryhausen. It’s actually based on the best-selling non-fiction ufology book “Flying Saucers from Outer Space” by Donald Keyhoe, and the film is smart in invoking a documentary-like aesthetics decades before the concept of “mockumentary” becomes popular. Even if the film is not that well-known nowadays, it’s one of the most influential films of the atomic era.
[previewyoutube=2o4fdX8gUMY;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]FORBIDDEN PLANET (1956)[/h1]

Fred M. Wilcox’s Forbidden Planet is one of the biggest classics of science fiction, and Robby the Robot might be even more of an icon than the film itself. It’s one of the first films to be set entirely in interstellar scenery, and to feature faster-than-light space travel. The groundbreaking Oscar-nominated visual effects show us that there was nothing “B” about this one by the time it was released. This film is a milestone for science-fiction and it’s been present in popular culture ever since.
[previewyoutube=AxQ9GG6hUDM;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]THE WAR OF THE WORLDS (1953)[/h1]

This one is probably the most famous sci-fi movie of the 1950’s, mainly because the book in which is based was already a classic for half a century by the time the movie hit theaters. H. G. Wells’ novel tells us about the martian invasion on planet Earth and it was published when the British Empire was expanding its dominance, and is widely interpreted as an allegory for European imperialism.

Before the film, it also inspired a radio sensation when Orson Welles narrated the facts described in the book as broadcast news in 1938, allegedly causing panic among the audience on the brink of World War II. 
[previewyoutube=9q7tN7MhQ4I;full][/previewyoutube]

In the 1950’s, however, the Oscar-winning film was released and it reframed its meanings to the Cold War paranoia and helped define alien iconography for generations.
[previewyoutube=ANqr3wVKaD8;full][/previewyoutube]

More recently, another adaptation showed the power of H. G. Wells’ novel to reframe itself to the changes of the political zeitgeist when Steven Spielberg retold the story in a post-9/11 context in the Tom Cruise vehicle also named “War of the Worlds” (2005).

[h1]GODZILLA (1954)[/h1]

At the same time American science-fiction of the 1950’s was expressing the fears of Cold War and communist paranoia, the greatest Japanese kaiju classic was mourning the consequences of atomic violence. Godzilla established the template for kaiju films and tokusatsu media for ages. In the film, the Japanese authorities are dealing with the sudden appearance of a giant lizard-like monster that was awaken by nuclear explosions. It became not only the greatest monster movie of all time, but also a beloved symbol, a franchise with almost 40 films, not to mention all the classic hits it inspired in the west, such as “Jurassic Park” (1993) and "Cloverfield" (2010).
[previewyoutube=KNmk4uTZ6vI;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Update #03 THEM! Meet Cast and Crew #02 - The Villains!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38472313/87dfdcd7c64910795c3dc5486a3fbb31856017e9.png[/img]

Today we celebrate the actors who played the villains of “Squadron 51”. Under an astounding characterization, achieved by makeup FX and costume design, those actors brought to life the dreadful antagonists, be they alien or human.

Director Zarog is the leader of the extraterrestrials, manager of the headquarters of the Vega Corporation, the enterprise responsible for the flying saucer’s invasion. He’s played by Cristian Verardi, who is no less than an horror icon in brazillian film circles. You can’t tell by looking at him characterized as an alien villain, but Cristian is not only an actor, but a writer, a poet, a literature graduate, a film critic and festival curator. As a film director, he had his short film “Ne Pas Projeter” played in some of the biggest horror film festivals in the world, like SITGES. During the pandemic, Cristian became also a great Instagrammer, producing content related to horror films and literature, as you can check in @cristianverardi and @avingancadosfilmesb.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38472313/74cb3af3737e33912cfe9507e64887ee682ae9b9.png[/img]

He is accompanied by his loyal and stoic alien Advisor. This one is played by the great Frederico Vittola, an experienced theater actor and musician, with a lot of feature films and TV shows under his belt, such as the horror series “Desalma” (2020) and the historic drama “Resistance” (2019). You can check more of his work in his official website, https://www.fredericovittola.com/

The extraterrestrial plans are only successful because they count with the help of Colonel Bob, an old-school media baron on the likes of William Hearst and Roberto Marinho. A lesser-charming Citizen Kane that becomes Zarog’s lapdog, Bob is responsible for manipulating public opinion on Squadron 51. We invited the renowned actor and comedian Oscar Simch to play the character. One of the most recognizable actors in our state, he’s known not only by his parts in big-scale productions, like the epic “A Casa das Sete Mulheres”, but also for his comedy spectacle “Homens de Perto”, that is being presented for more than 15 years now and counting.

Last, but not least, what is a villain without his minions? We’ve decided to look for twin actors to play the multitude of similar alien minions spread on Earth to protect the extraterrestrial facilities. Through a social networks research, we found the perfect duo. Arthur & Gabriel Chilante are not actors, though they had a little bit of experience in high school plays. Gabriel is currently studying to be a biologist when he’s not dungeon-mastering RPG campaigns, and we’re glad he could overcome his phobia of ETs to play one of ours. Arthur is studying to be an architect and is also a very skilled archer, which was very useful on set when he taught Paula Souza, the actress who plays Captain Zeferina, how to use a bow-and-arrow.

“We’re huge fans of classic sci-fi horror and we jumped at the opportunity to co-publish Squadron 51 with our partner WhisperGames,”[/i] said Assemble Entertainment CEO Stefan Marcinek. [i]“Squadron 51 has found a loving home among Assemble Entertainment’s other award-winning titles known for their charming eccentricity. notes.title: ATTACK FROM PLANET TRIVIA #02
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38472313/97cac00c1f139a855f1c708949a69752a34ed633.png[/img]

Squadron 51 is being developed in Rio Grande do Sul, on the very south of Brazil, very near to the frontier with Uruguai. Coincidence or not, is no surprise that an UFO-themed videogame has its roots here, since it's historically one of the favorite spots for extraterrestrials to visit here in Brazil.

There's been a lot of UFO activity in Brazil throughout the decades, from the mysterious incidents in the Amazon forest in the 1970s, supposedly covered up by the military dictatorship, to the infamous close encounters in Varginha city in the late 1990s.  But a lot of lesser-known incidents happened very near from the headquarters of the developing studio Loomiarts and film company Fehorama Filmes. 

Here you'll find out about a few of the many cases that happened right here in our state, a region that also houses study centers for ufologists and places of interest for UFO-tourists. 

[h2]THE BERLET CASE (1958) 
[/h2]
In Sarandi (RS), tractor driver Artur Berlet claimed to have been taken away by a flying saucer on May 14, 1958. He only returned 11 days later. At the time, the abduction case was known worldwide. The tractor driver's account was rich in detail. He was reportedly taken to the planet Acart, 65 million kilometers from Earth, and the trip would have lasted 38 hours. Acartians supposedly had a physical type similar to humans and communicated with him in German. Berlet's account was published in the book "From Utopia to Reality, a real trip to another planet".

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38472313/11af382548810869c8c651987e8d4ce306de0b14.jpg[/img]

[h2]THE WESTENDORFF CASE (1996)[/h2]
In Saragonha Island, at Lagoa dos Patos, the airplane pilot Haroldo Westendorff witnessed a cone-shaped (or is it pyramid-shaped?) UFO, 50 to 60 meters tall, with a base as big as a soccer stadium. He flew around the object for 15 minutes, keeping 100 meters of distance. The object was spinning around itself and heading towards the sea and was spotted at the radar of Pelotas' airport. Westendorff also reported a smaller object coming out of the top of the big UFO, which climbed into the skies at a very fast speed, with the larger UFO following shortly afterwards.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38472313/6a6afcd091676fff0181adf27ca9571b945d8255.jpg[/img]

[h2]THE SANTO ANGELO CASE (1997) [/h2]
On February 25, 1997, in Santo Ângelo, the resident Vanda Polansky was with her family when they noticed something that sounded like a motorcycle engine. After going out the door to check, Vanda found spheres of red lights that went up to the sky and disappeared. At the time, the Porazzis, Vanda's neighbors, also confirmed the sighting. The family saw a strong flash that would have originated the phenomenon observed by Vanda. About five people witnessed the case, and afterwards, even crop circles and dead bugs were found nearby. 

[h2]THE 2020 LIGHT SPHERES (2020)[/h2]
Even in 2020, in the midst of the Covid-19 pandemic, the extraterrestrials couldn’t help to step by. In the night of June 22, the entrepreneur Rudinei and his daughter Giovana, witnessed the presence of light spheres on the skies in the north coast of Rio Grande do Sul. At first, they thought it was a shooting star or maybe some unusual fireworks, but then, as it got brighter and started to move randomly, they realized it couldnt’ be any of that. They even photographed it. They weren’t alone in their account: another dozens of people told the same otherworldly stories on social networks in the same week, in different beaches.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38472313/eef236d38e56548d7be47ba488487ef53a8a018c.jpg[/img]

[h2]M. NIGHT SHYAMALAN's SIGNS (2002)[/h2]
Even the film director M. Night Shyamalan, known for the classic The Sixth Sense (1999), noticed our state's fame of welcoming alien invasors, and decided to use a city in Rio Grande do Sul as the spot where one of the first close encounters with aliens took place in his film "Signs" (2002). You can check it out here in this scene where Joaquin Phoenix's character is watching news on TV, when he's astounded by an extraterrestrial appearance at a children's party in Passo Fundo (Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil).

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HeTjBPbY70Y

In this segment, we're proud to introduce members from our cast and crew that are helping us to build the universe and narrative of our Squadron 51.

We're starting with João França, who played the glorious Major Ivan in both cinematics and voice acting during gameplay. Almost everyone who graduated in film school in our state, Rio Grande do Sul, worked with him at some point. João França had been working as an actor since 1990. Since then, he worked on a lot of films and theater plays, and gave his great voice to a number of videogames and commercials.

notes.title: ATTACK FROM PLANET TRIVIA #01
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38472313/b3b934d437b0c726759483482b79936adde1513d.png[/img]

If you’ve watched the trailers and behind-the-scenes videos we’ve been sharing, you might’ve noticed the 6-star emblem in our aircrafts, which is also seen in the armbands of our pilots.

As many details in Squadron 51’s lore, this emblem points to Brazil’s colonial past and to the centuries of resistance and fight for freedom that define our history. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38472313/d977dc77d38544a7a0da13319dee45a62bf0afe6.png[/img]

In the late 18th century, while the French Revolution and the American Revolutionary War were taking place, the illuminist ideals were also reaching Brazil, influencing small revolts spread across the country, with significant differences from one to another, but they all faced tragic consequences and violent repression.

The most famous one was “Inconfidência Mineira”, organized mainly by wealthy white men, and is widely celebrated around the brazillian icon of "Tiradentes". But there were others, that unfortunately are constantly reduced to footnotes in our history books.

One of those was “Conjuração Baiana” or “The Tailors’ Revolt”. It’s called this way because it had a strong participation of lower-class workers, such as tailors, shoemakers, seamstresses and also slaves and those who were already been granted freedom. Influenced not only by Illuminism, but also by the Haitian Revolution, this was one of the movements organized mainly by black leaders and, as often happens in our history, it does not always get all the attention it deserves.

It was a popular revolt that started in Salvador, Bahia, triggered by the dire conditions that workers found themselves, high taxes and increasing hunger among those in more vulnerable situations, not to mention the egalitarian, republican and abolitionist ideals that drove them to rise against the Portuguese monarchy that controlled Brazilian economy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38472313/d9701e49307b7d12c52ab4ec2ba8c5cad212e0a6.png[/img]

The six-star flag of “Conjuração Baiana” represents the 06 main ideals of this rebellion:

[list]
[*] Abolition of slavery
[*] End of prejudice
[*] Proclamation of the Republic
[*] Lower taxes
[*] Opening of Seaports
[*] Wage increase
[/list]

One of the mottos seen in the revolutionary pamphlets said:

“Cheer up, people of Bahia, that the happy time of our freedom is coming soon: the time in which we shall all be brothers, the time in which we shall all be equals”.


We’re using the six-star flag as a homage to this underrated moment in our History, as it’s perfectly aligned with the ideals of Squadron 51, an organization that fights against all Director Zarog stands for. We, as a team, believe that spreading this ideals is a way to try to defeat the Director Zarogs across the World.


The Squadron 51’s emblem is one of the aspects in our project where we mix the 1950s Hollywoodian references with those details of our colonial history to create an unique lore!
